items.heading: Government Roles Are Genuinely Different
items.text: Government roles are genuinely different from private-sector or skill-based paths in ways that matter more than the "safe versus risky" headline most people default to. Structured pay bands, defined promotion cycles, pension-linked retirement benefits, and a selection process that does not depend on office politics or a manager's mood are real, concrete advantages, not just a feeling of safety.

items.heading: You Are Drawn
items.text: You are drawn to the actual nature of the work, structure, public service, a defined process, not just its reputation.

items.heading: Not Government Versus Private
items.text: Not government versus private in the abstract, the specific things worth weighing against your own situation.

items.heading: The Expensive Mistake Is Not
items.text: The expensive mistake is not choosing government over private, it is spending a year or more preparing for a specific exam before honestly testing whether the government path fits your risk tolerance, income goals, and family reality at all.

items.heading: Genuine Fit and Pressure
items.text: Genuine fit and pressure-driven fit look similar from the outside. The pull toward public service and structured stability is a real fit signal; the pull toward avoiding the private-sector job search or a hard family conversation is not.

items.heading: Once Government Exams Become
items.text: Once government exams become the settled plan, the next-stage decisions, which exams, whether to run several in parallel, what to do after a non-selection, are a separate, more exam-specific kind of guidance.
